If your Pune business gets most of its real enquiries by phone, Google Ads call tracking is how you find out which keywords and ads produce calls worth answering, and which only produce ringing. The short version: add call assets to your ads, turn on call reporting so that calls from ads are counted using Google forwarding numbers, add website call tracking if you want to know which ad led to a call after a visit to your site, count only calls above a sensible minimum length as conversions, and then check a sample of the actual calls to see whether they were customers. A digital marketing agency in Pune that reports "calls" without doing the last step is reporting activity, not results.

This article is for owners of clinics, coaching classes, repair and installation services, interior designers, event companies, packers and movers, and any local service business where the phone is the main way a lead arrives. It explains the three kinds of call you can get from Google Ads, what each setting actually tracks, how to set a conversion threshold, how to keep the numbers on your website and Google Business Profile consistent, what to do about call recording and consent, and how to review the result without trusting a dashboard blindly. It gives no promised cost per call, because that depends on your category, your location and your competition, and anyone quoting a figure before seeing your account is guessing.

## Why "number of calls" is a weak measure on its own

A call is not a lead. Calls include existing customers, wrong numbers, job seekers, salespeople, people asking for something you do not offer, and callers who hang up on the greeting. If an account is optimised to maximise the count of calls, the bidding system learns whatever pattern produces calls most cheaply, and that is often a pattern of short, low-intent calls.

Three layers of measurement fix this, and each answers a different question.

1. **Did the call happen, and from which ad?** This is call tracking proper.
2. **How long did it last?** A conversion threshold filters out the obvious non-leads.
3. **Was it a genuine enquiry, and did it become work?** This is lead quality, which needs a human, a CRM or both. Our article on [lead quality and offline conversions](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-lead-quality-offline-conversions-2026) goes deeper on closing this loop.

## The three types of phone lead Google Ads can produce

### 1. Calls from ads

When your ad shows a phone number, using a call asset (earlier known as a call extension) or an older call-only format, a person on a phone can tap the number and call you directly from the search results page. Google can substitute a Google forwarding number for your real one so that it can record that the call came from the ad, how long it lasted, and a few other details such as the caller's area code. Call reporting is a setting you must turn on; it is not automatic in every account.

Google has been moving advertisers away from call-only ads towards responsive search ads with call assets. What your account can create changes over time, so check the current options in the Google Ads interface and its help pages rather than assuming an old tutorial is current.

### 2. Calls from your website after an ad click

Someone clicks your ad, reads your page, and then calls the number printed on it. Without extra setup, Google Ads cannot connect that call to the click, because the number on your page is just a number. To count these, Google offers a website call conversion tag. It swaps the number shown to a visitor who arrived from an ad for a Google forwarding number, so the call can be matched to the click. This is sometimes called dynamic number insertion.

### 3. Clicks on a phone number on mobile

On a phone, a tap on a click-to-call link or button can be recorded as a conversion in its own right, by adding an event snippet to the link. This counts taps, not calls that connected. A tap and a completed call are different things, and the difference matters when you read the report. Our guide on [call and WhatsApp buttons for service websites](/blog/website-designer-pune-click-to-call-whatsapp-buttons-mobile-service-website-2026) covers the button design side, including how to track taps separately.

| Source of the call | What is tracked | Needs a forwarding number | Needs a tag on your site | Typical blind spot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Call asset on the ad | Call duration, start time, caller area code | Yes | No | Calls placed without tapping the ad number |
| Call after visiting your website | Call matched to the ad click and keyword | Yes | Yes | Visitors who write the number down and call later from another device |
| Tap on click-to-call button | The tap only | No | Yes (event snippet) | Taps that never connect |
| Call to your Google Business Profile | Reported in the Business Profile, not as an ad click | Depends on settings | No | Cannot be attributed to a specific search ad |

Exact names and screens inside Google Ads change from time to time, so treat the table as the logic of what is measured rather than a click path.

## Setting up call reporting, step by step

The interface labels change, but the sequence is stable.

1. **Decide which number the ads will use.** Use a number that a person answers during business hours. A call asset that points to a number that goes to voicemail wastes the budget.
2. **Add a call asset to your campaign or account.** Enter the number, choose the country, and set a schedule that matches the hours you can actually answer. Showing a phone number outside those hours invites missed calls.
3. **Enable call reporting for the asset.** This is the setting that allows Google forwarding numbers to be used so the account can see call duration and source.
4. **Create a conversion action for "calls from ads".** Choose a minimum call length (explained below) and a counting method (usually "one" per customer for lead generation, so the same person calling three times does not look like three leads).
5. **If you want website call tracking, create the "calls to a phone number on your website" conversion.** Install the Google tag if it is not already present, and add the supplied snippet to the pages where the number appears. Test that the number on the page changes for a visitor who arrives from an ad.
6. **If you use a tap-to-call button, create a separate conversion for clicks on the number.** Give it a different name from the call conversion and decide whether it should be a primary conversion that bidding optimises for, or a secondary one for observation only.
7. **Place a test call.** Click your own ad on a phone, call the number, stay on for longer than the threshold, and check in the account that a conversion is recorded after the normal reporting delay. Do not click your own ads repeatedly, as that wastes the budget and can distort data.
8. **Write the setup down.** Record which numbers are in use, which conversions are primary, and what the threshold is. When an agency changes, this note is worth more than any dashboard.

## Choosing the minimum call length

Google's default minimum for a call to count as a conversion is 60 seconds for calls from ads. That default is a reasonable starting point, not a rule for your business. Consider the type of enquiry:

- **A booking line where a call takes 90 seconds.** A threshold of 60 seconds works.
- **A complex service where a proper enquiry takes several minutes.** A higher threshold, say 120 seconds, may filter better.
- **A quick yes-or-no business such as a pharmacy availability check.** A shorter threshold, and a different success measure altogether, may be needed.

The honest way to choose is to listen to a sample of calls. Check forty or fifty calls at different durations and note the length below which almost nothing useful occurs. That is your threshold. Revisit after a quarter. The point is not to find an exact number but to avoid counting 8-second wrong numbers as conversions.

If you also track website forms, keep the call conversions and form conversions distinct so you can see the split. A reader who wants to improve the form side may find our article on [Google Ads assets such as sitelinks and callouts](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-google-ads-assets-sitelinks-callouts-lead-generation-2026) useful, since call assets belong to the same family.

## Keep your numbers consistent across the website and Google Business Profile

Local search trust depends partly on consistent business details. If you use tracking numbers, be careful about where they appear.

- Keep one real, answered number as your main number on your website's contact page, footer and structured data, and on your Google Business Profile. Our article on [LocalBusiness schema, name, address and phone consistency](/blog/web-development-company-pune-localbusiness-schema-nap-opening-hours-2026) covers why.
- Use tracking numbers only where you intend to measure a particular source, and, where a profile allows it, list your main number as primary and a tracking number as additional. Check the current Business Profile guidelines when you do this, because the rules on what is allowed have changed over the years.
- Do not swap the number on pages that Google crawls into something different for every visitor in a way that shows crawlers a number that is not your business number. Dynamic number replacement is designed to show a forwarding number only to visitors from ads, with your real number as the default.
- If you run ads for several services through different tracking numbers, record which number belongs to which campaign in a shared sheet.

## Call recording, consent and privacy

Some call analytics tools record the audio of calls. Recording a customer call raises consent and data-protection questions. India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and its rules apply to personal data processed in digital form, and a voice recording of an identifiable person is personal data. We are not lawyers and this article is not legal advice; ask your own advisor how the rules apply to you. Practically, sensible practice looks like this:

- Tell callers at the start that the call may be recorded for quality and training, either through the greeting or a short announcement.
- Record only if you will use the recordings, for example to train staff or to review lead quality, and delete them on a set schedule.
- Restrict access to recordings to the people who need them.
- Do not record calls about sensitive matters such as health, unless your advisor confirms you have a lawful basis and appropriate consent.
- If you use a third-party call tracking tool, check where its data is stored and what its terms say about use of the recordings.

Google's call reporting does not record the audio of calls by default. It reports metadata such as duration and start time. Recording typically comes from a separate call tracking or call analytics product, which you would choose and configure on purpose.

## Handle the call, not only the click

Tracking tells you a call happened. It cannot make anyone pick up. Many small businesses lose more leads at the answering stage than at the advertising stage.

- **Missed calls.** Decide who answers during ad hours and what happens when they cannot. A missed call from an ad is a paid click wasted. A callback within a few minutes, or an automated WhatsApp message offering a callback slot, recovers some of them. See our article on [lead response speed and follow-up workflow](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-lead-response-speed-follow-up-workflow-2026) for a simple routine.
- **Greeting.** The person answering should know the call came from an ad for a particular service, and say something that confirms the caller is in the right place.
- **A log.** Keep a simple record for each call: date, service enquired, outcome. A shared spreadsheet is enough to start. A CRM is better once volume grows; our [CRM services](/whatsapp/crm) are built for this kind of follow-up.
- **After hours.** Either schedule the call asset to show only during staffed hours, or give callers an easy alternative such as a WhatsApp message or a form.

## A worked example, with assumptions marked

The following is an illustration with invented round numbers, not a benchmark and not a result from any client.

Suppose a Pune clinic spends a monthly budget on Google Search ads and the account reports 100 conversions of "call from ad" with no minimum duration. After setting a 60-second minimum and turning on form tracking separately, the account reports 38 call conversions and 22 form conversions. The 62 calls removed were mostly wrong numbers, existing patients asking for opening hours, and hang-ups. The clinic then listens to a sample of the 38 and finds that most are genuine appointment enquiries.

What changed is not the performance of the ads. What changed is that the reporting now describes something closer to reality, and the bidding system now learns from a stricter signal. If cost per reported conversion rises after the change, that does not mean the ads got worse; it means the earlier number was flattering. The lesson is to expect the headline number to fall when you tighten the definition, and to judge the change by the quality of the calls, not by the count.

## Reading the report without fooling yourself

When you review the numbers monthly, ask these questions in order:

1. How many calls from ads were there, and how many met the duration threshold?
2. Which campaigns and keywords produced them? Look at search terms, not only keywords, and add irrelevant ones as negatives. See our guide to [search terms and negative keywords](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-search-terms-negative-keywords-2026).
3. At what hours and on which days did calls arrive, and how many were answered?
4. Of a sample of at least twenty calls, how many were real enquiries and how many became customers?
5. What did each real enquiry cost, using total spend divided by the number of real enquiries from your own log?
6. Did anything change in the account, such as a new asset, a changed threshold or a paused campaign, that explains a jump?

The number from question five is the one you should compare against what a customer is worth. The platform cannot calculate it for you, because it does not know which calls became sales.

## Common mistakes

- Counting every call from ads regardless of length.
- Tracking taps on a button as if they were connected calls.
- Pointing a call asset to a number nobody answers.
- Turning on website call tracking without testing that the number swap works on every device and page template.
- Letting a tracking number replace the main number across the whole site, including structured data.
- Recording calls without telling callers.
- Judging the account on the platform's count without listening to a single call.
- Changing the threshold or conversion settings mid-month and then comparing with the previous month as if nothing changed.
- Making a primary conversion out of something very easy to trigger, which teaches the bidding system to chase cheap, low-value actions.

## When a call-first strategy is the wrong choice

For some businesses calls are not the best goal. If your team cannot answer reliably, if your customers prefer messaging, or if you sell to people who research for days before enquiring, a form, a WhatsApp conversation or a booking page may suit better. For businesses that sell to a younger or office-based audience, a call can be a barrier. The right approach is to offer both and let the data show which your customers choose, which is what the first 90 days of a local campaign is for; our piece on the [first 90 days for a local business](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-first-90-days-local-business-plan-2026) describes the sequence. If you use click-to-WhatsApp ads, the measurement logic differs, and our [WhatsApp ads and automation pages](/whatsapp/click-to-whatsapp-ads) explain it.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can Google Ads track phone calls from my ads?
Yes. With call assets and call reporting turned on, Google can use forwarding numbers to report calls from ads, including their duration. Calls from your website after an ad click need a separate website call conversion tag, and taps on a phone number on mobile need an event snippet.

### How long should a call be to count as a conversion?
Google's default for calls from ads is 60 seconds, which is a sensible starting point. Choose your own threshold by listening to a sample of calls and finding the length below which few are genuine enquiries, then review it every quarter.

### Does call tracking change the phone number on my website?
Only if you use website call tracking. In that setup, visitors who arrive from an ad see a Google forwarding number, while everyone else sees your normal number. Keep your real number as the default and on your Google Business Profile.

### Do I need to tell callers that I am recording?
Tell them. Recording a customer's voice involves personal data, and clear notice is good practice under India's data protection rules. Ask your legal advisor about your specific situation, and record only what you will use.

### Why are my reported calls lower after I set a minimum duration?
Because very short calls, such as wrong numbers and hang-ups, are no longer counted. The ads did not get worse; the measurement got stricter. Judge the change by the quality of the calls you answer, not by the headline count.

## Where to Start

This week, listen to ten recent calls from your ads, or ask whoever answers the phone to list the last ten. Count how many were genuine enquiries. That one number tells you whether the problem is your tracking, your ads or your answering process. If you want help setting up the conversions described above or reviewing an existing account, talk to the team.
